Nikhil — quick note. I forwarded your original .ics to Hiroto from my Gmail because he wasn't on the first thread. Gmail's forward sometimes strips the TZ property (it turns the event into a "floating" time: no TZ attached), which will cause local clients to interpret the timestamp in the recipient's default timezone. That's likely how his calendar jumped +1 hour.

Recommendation: don't attach the .ics. Instead create a new calendar event in Google Calendar and invite all attendees by email (that preserves the timezone anchor), and also paste the explicit UTC time in the body. I'll help with sending if you want me to (I can create the event from the account that has APAC region default).

Also: include the meeting link in the event (some clients ignore links when they parse floating events).

-Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
